overall: The AG found the committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve minutes for about a year and a half and by failing to complete member certification forms, and ordered compliance steps.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the committee failed to create and approve minutes for all open sessions from July 15, 2020 through December 6, 2021.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve meeting minutes for a year and a half.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged all committee members failed to complete the required Open Meeting Law certification form.
allegations.key_passage: Despite multiple requests from our office, the Committee has not provided copies of certification forms for any of its members.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Create and approve meeting minutes for all outstanding meetings to the best of its ability, using recordings, notes and attendee recollections, and certify compliance to the AG within 90 days.

All committee members review the Open Meeting Law, the AG's regulations and the Open Meeting Law Guide, and certify that they understand the requirements, filing with the superintendent and emailing copies to the AG within 14 days.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee to create and approve meeting minutes for all outstanding meetings to the best of its ability, through whatever means are available, including recordings and the notes and recollections of the attendees.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
